stem.text: Let f be a twice-differentiable function with \( f(1) = -1 \) and \( f'(x) = x^{2} - 8 \) for all x. Use the line tangent to the graph of f at x = 1 to approximate \( f(1.2) \). Is this approximation an overestimate or an underestimate of \( f(1.2) \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The approximation is \( -2.4 \), and it is an underestimate, because \( f''(x) = 2 x \) is positive for x > 0, so the graph of f is concave up and lies above its tangent line there.

worked_solution.text: The slope of the tangent line is \( f'(1) = -7 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: slope of the tangent line from the derivative

worked_solution.text: The tangent line at x = 1 is \( y = -1 - 7(x - 1) \).

worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the tangent line at the nearby input

worked_solution.text: \( f''(x) = 2 x \), which is positive for every x between 1 and 1.2. The graph is concave up there, so it lies above the tangent line and the approximation is an underestimate.
worked_solution.rule_named: concavity decides the direction of the error
